title: An environment for a notebook: libraries, resources and the default environment
objective_text: Put public and custom libraries and a small data file in the right parts of an environment, publish it the right way, and make it the workspace default.
scenario: The sales team's notebooks each pip-install what they need at the top, and runs break when a package changes. You're moving everything into one environment, but the draft has the wheel and the CSV swapped and was never published.

rules.why: Library and compute changes take effect only after you save and publish.
Full mode makes a stable, reproducible library snapshot; Quick mode installs libraries when a session starts.

hints: Which part of an environment is for code you install, and which for small files you read?
When do library changes take effect?
Which publish mode gives a reproducible snapshot?
explanation: An environment holds Spark compute settings, libraries and resources. Public libraries come from sources such as PyPI and custom libraries are files you upload; resources are small files notebooks read, and change without a publish. Library and compute changes apply only once published. Full mode builds a stable snapshot, which suits production; Quick mode publishes fast and installs libraries as each session starts. Making the environment the workspace default saves attaching it to every notebook.
